q: How does CBAM treat gas-fired captive power at a UAE aluminium smelter such as those at Al Taweelah?
title: UAE smelter gas power and CBAM
short: The emissions from generating the smelter's electricity, even in its own gas-fired plant, are indirect emissions and are not charged for aluminium under CBAM today. The charge covers direct emissions: anode consumption, perfluorocarbons from anode effects and fuel burnt on site, plus any precursor aluminium.
audience: Aluminium smelters, casthouses and their EU buyers in the UAE and the wider Gulf

ul: In: CO2 from carbon anodes consumed in electrolysis.
In: CF4 and C2F6 from anode effects, using the GWPs in the CBAM rules.
In: fuel for anode baking, casthouse furnaces and other on-site heat.
Out of the charge: emissions from producing the electricity, whether from the grid or a captive gas plant.

sections.h: Why it matters for Gulf metal
p: Gulf smelters run on gas-fired power, which emits far less per MWh than coal but far more than hydro. Under Annex II only direct emissions are charged, so the CBAM figures of a gas-powered and a coal-powered smelter can be close, while their full footprints differ widely. EU buyers counting Scope 3 will see that difference.
Article 9 allows a deduction only for a carbon price effectively paid on the emissions. Where no carbon price applies at the smelter, nothing is deducted.
